clue.text: Secretary twisted neck catching a small bit of 15

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; here only its second word counts, so a bit of it is one dish

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of its natural shape, so these letters are rearranged
to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece closes round another

blocks.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary
the four letters of the word, rearranged
taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An office secretary with a cricked neck manages to grab a small piece of the TV equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout the puzzle 15 (SATELLITE DISH) is split: some answers are satellites, others dishes. 'Twisted neck' sounds like an injury, but it only scrambles four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancakes are a food served on a plate, so they qualify as one example of a dish.

clue.text: New York look essentially retranslates legwear

indicators.note: the essence of something lies at its core, so only the central letters are used

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for the city or state
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
the twelve-letter word has these two letters at its centre

explanation.surface: A New York fashion look gets translated again into the language of hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is the archaic 'look!', a crossword staple; a twelve-letter word has two middle letters, here NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings made from the synthetic fibre, worn on the legs, hence an item of hosiery.

clue.text: Diamonds wow, encrusted with proper gemstone

indicators.note: a crust forms a covering layer, so one piece is wrapped around the others

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
cor is a British exclamation of surprise
proper in the sense of genuine, the real thing

explanation.surface: A jeweller admires diamonds set in a genuine precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds' reads as the gems in the setting, but it is just the card-suit abbreviation. 'Cor!' is everyday British slang for 'wow!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Red coral is a precious organic material polished and set in jewellery, treated as a gem.

clue.text: Table setter starts to skip accoutrements

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so each following word contributes only that

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone laying a table skips the extra trimmings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table setter' looks like a person laying cutlery, but the definition is just 'Table' and 'setter' is the compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill, a tableland; it is also the Spanish word for a table.

clue.text: Electric vehicle put in dreary gorge

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside another thing

blocks.note: EV is the standard abbreviation
dour means gloomy and severe

explanation.surface: An electric car is driven into a gloomy ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a canyon for the car to sit in, but it is the verb meaning to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge and to devour are both verbs for eating food hungrily and in large amounts.

clue.text: 15 feature about priest and rabbi on vacation

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; the feature meant is a dish

indicators.note: vacating a place leaves it empty, so the word loses its insides and keeps its ends

blocks.note: ca is circa, Latin for about
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A TV feature about a priest and a rabbi taking a holiday together.
explanation.walkthrough: '15 feature' suggests a programme on the satellite dish, but only its 'dish' half is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is fried squid served as a starter, so it is one example of a restaurant course.

clue.text: Portion of 15 shows blocked by head of ITV1

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; the portion meant is a satellite

indicators.note: a blockage sits inside a passage, so one piece lodges within the other
the head is the top, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: demos are demonstrations, things that show how something works
the opening letter of the channel name

explanation.surface: Programmes from the satellite feed get interrupted by ITV1's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV1 is a British television channel, which suits the satellite TV surface. 'Portion of 15' here means the satellite half.
explanation.definitionFit: Deimos is the smaller of the two moons of Mars, a natural satellite of that planet.

clue.text: 15’s beginning mean edgy broadcast

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; only the satellite half is meant

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters something widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A satellite channel's launch is a nasty, edgy broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the opening as '15 is beginning [from]': the themed satellite starts as a rearranged 'mean edgy'. 'Broadcast' suits the TV surface but scatters letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede is the largest moon of Jupiter, a natural satellite orbiting that planet.

clue.text: Polish fish nets repulsed island

indicators.note: a net encloses whatever it catches, so one piece surrounds another
something repulsed is driven back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: an eel is a long fish
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A Polish fish catch is pushed back from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' masquerades as the nationality; capitalised at the start, it is the coating. The Isle of Man is a British Crown dependency.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy coating, and nail polish is also called nail enamel, so the nouns match.

clue.text: Energy hack not quite sound on reflection

indicators.note: falling just short of complete means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
to hack is to chop

explanation.surface: An energy-saving tip that, thinking it over, doesn't quite hold up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound on reflection' sounds like 'reasonable when thought about', but it describes noise bouncing off a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is noise heard again after it bounces back from a wall or cliff.

clue.text: Standard design company advanced toward agriculture sector?

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for company
A is a common abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
the preposition to is a plain synonym of toward, as in walking to the door
farms make up the agricultural sector of an economy

explanation.surface: A design firm with a standard template moves into farming work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as 'ordinary', but it is a flag or banner, which carries heraldic devices.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of arms is the heraldic emblem displayed on a banner, so it is what a flag's pattern shows.

clue.text: Gherkin, maybe pickle-filled dairy product

indicators.note: something filled has contents put inside it

blocks.note: a pickle and a scrape are both awkward predicaments
skyr is a thick Icelandic cultured dairy product like yoghurt

explanation.surface: A gherkin sounds like part of a sandwich with pickle and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gherkin is the nickname of 30 St Mary Axe, a pickle-shaped office tower in London; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gherkin is a very tall City of London office block, an instance of a high-rise tower.

clue.text: Mate hoards most of his bottle

indicators.note: most but not all means one letter is dropped from the end
hoarding means keeping things stored inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a pal is a friend or mate
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A friend squirrels away most of a man's bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His bottle' looks like a possessive phrase, but 'his' is fodder and 'bottle' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass vial for medicine or perfume, a little container like a flask.

clue.text: Too American to lead English orchestra

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: An American is appointed conductor of an English orchestra as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To lead' places A in front. The London Symphony Orchestra is one of Britain's leading orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and also are both adverbs meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: It has tellies working when feed in back's plugged in

definitions.text: It has tellies working when feed in back's plugged in

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken
working implies being processed and kneaded, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, the first twelve letters of the mix
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A home-installer's note: the TVs only work once the cable feed is connected at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Plug the D into 'it has tellies' and rearrange. The whole clue also defines: a satellite dish keeps TVs working once its feed is connected. Tellies are televisions in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite dish is the receiving antenna that supplies broadcast signals to television sets through a cable connection.

clue.text: Withdrawal doesn't include boat purchase

indicators.note: leaving something out of a whole means those letters are removed

blocks.note: subtraction is taking away, a withdrawal
a sub is a submarine, a kind of boat

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a deal means the boat sale falls through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying the boat, but it means grip. Remove SUB from SUBTRACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or grip on a surface, which is exactly what traction provides.

clue.text: Ordinary night before beam sucks up yard

indicators.note: sucking something up draws it inside

blocks.note: the eve is the night before a special day
a ray is a beam of light
yd is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: On a normal night, a searchlight beam sweeps across the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Night before' gives EVE; the second 'before' simply places it ahead of the beam.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyday describes something commonplace and unremarkable, the adjective sense of ordinary.

clue.text: Perhaps hunters seem excited with horn

indicators.note: something excited is agitated and stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fox hunters get worked up at the sound of the hunting horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is split across 'seem' and 'horn', with 'excited' and 'with' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: People who ride to hounds on horseback are riders, one example of men on horses.

clue.text: Selection from 15 to try, finale first

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; the selection meant is a satellite

indicators.note: putting the finale first moves the closing letter round to the front

blocks.note: a judge tries or hears a case

explanation.surface: Pick something from the satellite menu to try, starting with the finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense: a court tries, or hears, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhea is the second largest moon of Saturn, so it is one of that planet's natural satellites.

clue.text: Opening welcome present for crossworders

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
present at something means there, at it
the solvers, from the setter's point of view, are us

explanation.surface: A welcome gift handed out to crossword fans at an opening event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening welcome present' reads as one phrase, a gift at a launch; the definition is 'Opening' alone, in the sense of gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or break in continuity, the noun sense of an opening between two parts.

clue.text: Part from 15, extracted quietly, works without casing

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; the part meant is a dish

indicators.note: removing the casing strips the outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: a tooth extracted is pulled
p is piano, quietly in music
the word with its first and last letters gone

explanation.surface: A component is quietly removed from the satellite dish, and its workings are exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part from 15' points to the 'dish' half; 'without casing' leaves the inside of 'works'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulled pork is slow-cooked shredded pork shoulder, served as a main course in barbecue cooking.

clue.text: Dwelling as The Beatles were in Hamburg?

definitions.text: Dwelling as The Beatles were in Hamburg?

blocks.note: surface reading: where the band were living during their Hamburg residency

blocks.clueFragment: as The Beatles were in Hamburg?
blocks.note: setter's reading: in Hamburg the band had not yet become the Fab Four, so they were before Fab; a dwelling of that name is a factory-built house

explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles were nicknamed the Fab Four, and played Hamburg clubs before their fame. Split the answer as PRE-FAB. Prefabs were quick-build houses common in post-war Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a house assembled from factory-made sections, so it is a kind of home.

clue.text: Piece of 15 snaps? Time to go for book

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; the piece meant is a satellite

indicators.note: one letter going so another can take its place signals a swap

blocks.note: snaps are photographs
T is the abbreviation for time
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Photos of the satellite dish? Time to make an album of them.
explanation.walkthrough: In PHOTOS the T is replaced by B. The question mark breaks the surface into two sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: Phobos is the larger of the two moons of Mars, a natural satellite of that planet.

clue.text: Let's act wildly, scheming in crass fashion

indicators.note: acting wildly is acting without order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a sly person is cunning and scheming

explanation.surface: A rallying call to run riot and plot crudely.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Let's' is ignored; only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something tactlessly means acting without sensitivity or delicacy, a crude and insensitive manner.

clue.text: Very high extremity of 15

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; the extremity meant is the dish that opens a meal

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
up means high, aloft

explanation.surface: The tip of a satellite dish mounted very high up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremity' suggests the rim of the dish on the roof; here it means a course at one end of a meal, the starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is traditionally served as the first course, so it sits at one end of a dinner menu.

clue.text: Hot spot not opening, as is web?

indicators.note: without its opening, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a web is woven, as by a spider

explanation.surface: A wifi hotspot that won't open, as the web sometimes does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot spot' and 'web' suggest internet access, but a web is spun or woven, and the hot spot is in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is an enclosed chamber heated for cooking, literally a place that is hot.

clue.text: Regret returning yearly to consume Oscar content from 15

definitions.note: 15 is SATELLITE DISH; the content meant is a satellite

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word runs from end to start
consuming takes something inside, so a letter goes within the pieces

blocks.note: to rue is to regret
pa is per annum, Latin for yearly
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Each year someone regrets binging Oscar-winning material off the satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar content' looks like award-winning programming, but the definition is 'content from 15'.
explanation.definitionFit: Europa is one of the four large Galilean moons of Jupiter, an icy natural satellite.

clue.text: University leaders retired unpaid, sans affirmation

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the van is the vanguard, those at the front
money unpaid is still owed

explanation.surface: Retired university heads, left without pay, receive no acknowledgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' is not about first letters: the van leads an army.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unavowed has never been openly declared or admitted, so it lacks any public confirmation.
